questions.q: What is the electrophile that attacks the ring in the Gattermann–Koch reaction?
questions.explain: CO is protonated by HCl and AlCl₃ takes up the chloride, giving HCO⁺. :CCl₂ belongs to Reimer–Tiemann and HC⁺=NH to the HCN version.

questions.q: Toluene is treated with CO and HCl in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃/CuCl. The major product is:
questions.explain: The methyl group activates the ring and directs ortho/para, and substitution goes mainly para, giving p-tolualdehyde. The –CHO goes on the ring, not on the side chain.

questions.q: Which compound does NOT undergo the Gattermann–Koch reaction?
questions.explain: The Gattermann–Koch reaction is not applicable to phenols and phenol ethers such as anisole; for these the HCN/HCl method or Reimer–Tiemann is used. Benzene and alkylbenzenes are the typical substrates.

questions.q: Why is a mixture of CO and HCl used instead of formyl chloride, the 'natural' Friedel–Crafts reagent for a –CHO group?
options: Formyl chloride would chlorinate the ring
Formyl chloride gives ketones instead of aldehydes
Formyl chloride does not react with AlCl₃
Formyl chloride is too unstable to isolate
questions.explain: HCOCl cannot be isolated, so CO + HCl is used to generate the formyl electrophile in situ. The modern view is that the formyl cation reacts directly.
